Operating-point target population mismatch (CONFIRMED, FLAG, non-blocking). FULL_READ_ONSETS_PER_WIN=27 is the ALL-onset full-read density (46034/1666=27.6). The audited G5a/G5b stratum bins ZERO-PRECEDING onsets only (exp19_floor.py:73,81; exp19_g5b_rebin.py:64-66), whose full-N density is ~8.5/win at width 300. Recomputed: targeting the stratum's own full-N density (~8.4 -> width ~550-600) still clears s6 but at ~1.2-1.6x, not the 3.6x headline. The binary PASS is invariant (s6 clears at every width >=450), only the 3.6x magnitude depends on the 27-target choice.

Wide-window run measures block-contiguity, not conversion strength (CONFIRMED, FLAG). Recomputed run-length reorders converters between widths (s6 is weakest at 300, 2nd-strongest at 1706), and s6's clearance rides a genuine but late plateau (~425k-500k) that is still elevated at the READ_AT=500k boundary. This is a robustness caveat on what the metric captures, not a manufactured pass: the floor genuinely collapses (full-data floor runs 7->2) and s6's plateau (windows 249-270, means 0.69-1.00) is genuinely far above band 0.64.
summary: The G5b window-artifact finding SURVIVES as a PASS; I could not break the central claim. Independently verified against code and by recompute: (1) the operating point (width 1706) is selected blindly on the null (min |onsets/win - 27|, a full-read constant; s6 absent from selection, exp19_g5b_rebin.py:136,47); (2) s6 clears the floor at EVERY width >=450 and is swallowed ONLY at the inherited 300-step window, a 6.7x range, so the width choice is non-pivotal and the pre-named falsifier cannot trigger; (3) the floor genuinely collapses -- floor seeds {1,3,7} have full-data longest runs of exactly 2 windows at width 1706 while s6 carries a real 22-window contiguous plateau (means 0.69-1.00, ~425k-500k), so widening is legitimate re-binning, not an oracle-gate that manufactures the effect; (4) cross-seed robustness reproduced exactly (seeds 719150/1/42/2026: floor_q99=5, s6_q10=18, s6_min 8-11 >= floor_max 7-8, 5/5 converters clear -- the worst s6 draw beats the best floor draw); (5) the band switch to 0.64 is the committed full-read C_shuffle detector (exp14_arms.py:161), not load-bearing (result invariant at 0.704). No CONFIRMED MUST-FIX. Three FLAGs ride alongside, all non-blocking: the '135-onset evidence requirement' is decorative (N_w reported but absent from the gate); the 27-onset operating-point target is the all-onset density while the audited stratum is zero-preceding (making the 3.6x headline magnitude target-dependent, though the binary PASS is invariant); and the wide-window metric measures block-contiguity riding a boundary-truncated plateau. The verdict, the pass, and the s6-clears conclusion are robust to all three.

operating-point-blindness.finding: The operating point (width 1706) is selected genuinely on the null, not on s6. exp19_g5b_rebin.py:136 chooses op = min over |onsets_per_window - FULL_READ_ONSETS_PER_WIN|, where FULL_READ_ONSETS_PER_WIN=27 is a full-read constant (line 47); s6 appears nowhere in the selection. Recomputed: |26.5-27|=0.5 (w1706) < |23.3-27|=3.7 (w1500) < |32.6-27|=5.6 (w2100), so 1706 wins on the null cleanly. Critically, the width choice cannot be doing the work: s6_clears_floor is true at EVERY width >=450 (450,600,900,1200,1500,1706,2100,3000 all true in the sweep json; only 300 false), a 6.7x range. For a null-based width to swallow s6, the anchor would have to land at width 300 (4.7 onsets/window), which would require asserting the full-read detector runs at ~5 onsets/window — contradicting the premise that the full read is dense (~27) and the stratum is the thinned/sparse arm. No defensible null value lands on the sole failing width. The pre-named falsifier did not trigger (floor_q99 collapses 10->5, s6 clears). Outcome-blindness holds; the concern is ruled out.

evidence-number.finding: The "~135-onset evidence requirement" the claim says it is "preserving" is inert in the certification. EVIDENCE_ONSETS=135 is arithmetically honest (5 windows x 27 onsets; band 0.64/N=5 provenance real at exp14_arms.py:161; full-read 46000/1666.7=27.6 checks), but it feeds ONLY N_w at exp19_g5b_rebin.py:120, which is placed into the reported row dict at :128 and consumed nowhere else. The gate is pure floor-separation: s6_clears_floor = s6_q10 > floor_q99 (:126) and conv_clears (:127); the operating point is chosen by onsets_per_window vs 27 (:136, not 135); the verdict uses only s6_clears_floor (:138-139). Setting EVIDENCE_ONSETS to any value leaves the verdict byte-identical. The claim's "preserving the ~135-onset evidence requirement" is therefore decorative. It does NOT falsify the central result: s6 clears floor 3.6x on separation regardless, s6 clears at all widths>=450 so OP choice is non-pivotal, and had 135/N_w been enforced as an absolute threshold it would have misfired (at 1706 N_w=5 <= floor_max=7, so non-converters would also meet it) — the code correctly uses separation instead. Framing overstatement, not a manufactured effect.

(4) 1706 is BEFORE the sep peak (2100=4.0 > 1706=3.6), not past the information-budget optimum, and s6 clears at every width >=450 including the sep-optimum 2100 - robust, not width-cherry-picked. These are robustness caveats, not a manufactured pass: the floor genuinely collapses (7->2 full data) and s6's plateau is genuinely far above 0.64.

wave-cache-faithfulness.finding: Re-bin faithfulness HOLDS — I could not break it. _cache_wave captures the correct zero-preceding onsets (recomputed n s0=14156=N_FULL exactly; post-acq strat 13847 ≈ preflight ~13800). _longest_run_binned bins correctly: window=wv//w, post-acq wv>=acq, empty windows break runs, per-window mean>=BAND; independent recompute (pinned seed 719150) reproduces the sweep JSON's central quantiles (w=300 floor_q99=10/s6_q10=9; w=1706 floor_q99~4-5/s6_q10=18). The thinning-base difference vs v1 (rebin thins full base 14156→keep 7915; v1 thins post-acq 13847→keep 7742) is NOT a defect: rebin discards pre-acq at bin time, so effective post-acq kept = keep*(n_post/n_full) reproduces v1's keep to within ~10 onsets for every seed including s6 (7804 vs 7817) — symmetric across converters/non-converters, no asymmetric inflation of s6 or deflation of floor. Only immaterial issue: a 1-of-~1600 window boundary offset (floor keeps [acq-EVAL,acq) via col>=acq; rebin drops raw wv<acq). If targeted to the stratum's own full-N density (~8.4→width~550-600) s6 still clears but ~1.2-1.6x not 3.6x. PASS survives (s6 clears at all widths>=450); the 3.6x headline depends on the 27-target choice.

divergence-mechanism.finding: The floor-shrinks-while-s6-grows divergence is genuine signal, not a re-binning artifact. Direct proof: binning s6's FULL (un-thinned) stratum at width 1706 exposes a sharply localized late episode (windows 248-270, region mean accuracy 0.876, individual windows 0.9-1.0) that dilutes to s6's 0.52 overall mean; floor seeds {1,3,7} have NO episode (longest full-data run = 2 windows each). Wide binning does not trivially inflate ALL runs: it averages chance fluctuations toward the uniform sub-band truth (floor washes to ~2 windows) while bridging s6's genuinely super-band contiguous stretch into one long run. That asymmetric response is the signature of a real finite-extent episode. The 'floor shrinks in window units' framing is unit-dependent (in onset units the floor GROWS 47->132->186), but the certification is a within-width comparison (s6_q10 vs floor_q99 at the same w) so m_w cancels — no unit cheat, and the separation ratio 3.6 is unit-invariant. No both-collapse at 3000 (s6_q10 12 vs floor 4 = 3.0x; s6's dip there is the finite episode extent being exceeded, still clearing). The pre-named falsifier (floor doesn't collapse AND s6 still fails) does not trigger.

band-switch.finding: The switch to band 0.64 is legitimate and NOT load-bearing. 0.64 is the actual committed full-read C_shuffle detector band (exp14_arms.py:161: X15_REPRO C_shuffle band=0.64, converters=[0,2,4,5,6]) — the very set the rebin classifies as converters (exp19_g5b_rebin.py:39) is defined by it. 0.704 is a DIFFERENT detector's constant: the s0-anchor episode-exclusion band S0_LEVEL/EPISODE_BAND (exp14_arms.py:83-84), which exp19_floor.py:47 itself labels 'the forced cap'. Decisive test: I recomputed the full outcome-blind sweep at BAND=0.704 (same seed 719150, K=2000, same evidence-preserving logic). At the operating-point width 1706 s6 STILL clears the floor decisively (s6_q10=15 > floor_q99=3, sep 5.0, 5/5 converters clear); at the inherited width 300 s6 is still swallowed (s6_q10=8 <= floor_q99=8, 4/5). s6 clears at every width >=450 at BOTH bands. The window-artifact conclusion and the pass are invariant to the band choice; the pre-named falsifier does not trigger at 0.704 either. If anything 0.64 is the more conservative band at the operating point (floor_q99 5/sep 3.6 vs floor_q99 3/sep 5.0 at 0.704), so the switch does not inflate s6 or deflate the floor. My 0.64 recompute bit-matches all 9 rows of the committed sweep JSON, validating the harness.
